inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio, VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For Ambient Clock (checked 2026-11-16): VisualCoreRendering has FullScreenShaderScene (parameters, palette up to 8 stops, seedOffsets, fixedTime, timeScale), FieldPass, ShaderBundle with the vc/ GLSL library, ParticleRenderer and ParticleLayerScene (brightnessCap); VisualCoreSimulation has SceneClock (animation time, not wall time), ParticleSystem, AnnouncementPlanner, StateSign, stateSignProblems, transitionDuration(_:reduceMotion:) and AccessibilityPreferences; VisualCorePersistence has NamedLibrary (favourites), DocumentStore, DocumentEnvelope and MigrationChain; VisualCoreExperience has ExperienceStorage with StorageQuota; VisualCoreDiagnostics has QualityProfile, QualityGovernor, DeviceConditions and FramePacing; VisualCoreUI has AccessibleColors.contrastRatio. Missing in every framework product (grep 2026-11-16): a wall-clock source, any time-change observer (significant time change, time zone, locale, day), GPU text, a crossfade between scenes, a frame-rate control reachable from an experience, keep-awake, night-mode and pixel-drift helpers.

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler (CADisplayLink, FramePacing cap: 30 fps floor, 30 under Low Power Mode or serious thermal state, else the requested maximum, 60 by default) and context generations; every GL call runs on the main thread inside RenderScene setup, resize, render and teardown. RenderHost pauses on didEnterBackground, resumes on willEnterForeground, rebuilds on memory warning and recreateContext, and swaps scenes with replaceScene (a hard cut). RenderHost.init takes maxFramesPerSecond, but ExperienceSession creates its host with the default, so no experience can lower its frame rate today.

inventory.area: Shaders and resources (full-screen shaders, fields, palettes, particles, text overlays)
inventory.description: FullScreenShaderScene draws one bundled fragment shader over the canvas with named float uniforms, a palette of up to 8 colour stops, seed offsets and an explicit or scaled time; FieldPass runs a fragment program into a render target or the framebuffer (with PingPongTarget for feedback); ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary compile bundled GLSL with #include of the vc/ library (palette, noise, sdf, hash, colour, field); ParticleSystem simulates on the CPU and ParticleRenderer/ParticleLayerScene draw it with blend modes, trails and a brightness cap; ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget. Text is never drawn in the GPU path: ExperiencePresenter.makeCanvasOverlay puts native SwiftUI text over the canvas, so system fonts, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver apply.

SceneClock is a bounded animation clock (play, pause, speed, reducedMotion factor 0.5), not a wall clock; FullScreenShaderScene.fixedTime renders a scene at an explicit time. Scene phase reaches an experience through ExperienceSession.setScenePhase (ScenePhaseInput) and ExperienceShell.suspend/resume, which resume without catch-up. No framework product reads Date(), the calendar, the locale or the time zone for an experience, and none observes significantTimeChange, NSSystemTimeZoneDidChange or currentLocaleDidChange. Experience-only precedents: Solar System Explorer's injected now: () -> Date with its date.set action, and the willEnterForeground observers of Music Lab, Oscilloscope Studio and Audio Odyssey.

AccessibilityPreferences resolves Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing against SystemAccessibility (observed by SystemAccessibilityObserver); AnnouncementPlanner rate-limits announcements and AnnouncementSink speaks them; StateSign and stateSignProblems keep information independent of colour; transitionDuration shortens animations under Reduce Motion; AccessibleColors.contrastRatio gives the WCAG ratio (1 to 21) of two colours. In-scene dimming exists only in Digital Aquarium (AmbientDimmer, public in its Core, A09-P05), which never touches the system brightness or the idle timer; no pixel-drift helper exists anywhere.

DocumentStore writes versioned documents (DocumentEnvelope kind and schemaVersion) atomically under a byte cap (maxBytes) and migrates them forward through a MigrationChain, reporting damaged or newer files as problems instead of crashing; NamedLibrary keeps named documents with save, duplicate, rename, setFavorite and delete, favourites first; ExperienceStorage is the experience's own folder with StorageQuota.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode), memory and scene-phase events, and keeps a PerformanceRecord (frame cap, render scale, GPU bytes) for measured claims; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls, canvas overlay through makeCanvasOverlay) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; ScenarioRunner replays a ScenarioManifest; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (seventeen registered, A01-A17, checked 2026-11-16; Ambient Clock joins in A18-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A18-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets). Version 0.1 needs no permission and no usage string.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 143 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-16 (shared checks including app-contracts, which checks every docs/apps/*/visualcore-contract.json, package and app builds and tests, experience-release and copy-claims steps of the released experiences, verify steps of A01-A17 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps and the ProjectM independence check). No release scan refuses isIdleTimerDisabled or a screen-brightness write today (grep of scripts/ 2026-11-16); the A18 release step adds one (G-RELEASE).

Ambient Clock owns its domain (clock preferences: 12/24 hours, seconds, calendar, time-zone and locale policy; the formatter and the full spoken time; the update schedule on second or minute boundaries and on time-change notifications; the four themes and their presets; the theme editor and favourite documents with their schema; night-mode, motion, screen-care and keep-awake policies; budgets per tier; copy) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/AmbientClock/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A18-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: full-screen shaders, fields, the GLSL library, particles and render targets (VisualCoreRendering), animation clocks and accessibility planning (VisualCoreSimulation), persistence (VisualCorePersistence), storage, digests and the host (VisualCoreExperience, VisualCoreExperienceHost), quality and pacing (VisualCoreDiagnostics). Solar System Explorer's injected clock, Digital Aquarium's AmbientDimmer and the foreground observers of other experiences stay experience code and are not copied. ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/ambient-clock/regression-baseline.md.

StateDigest fingerprints experience state so the same preferences, theme and injected date give the same digest; ScenarioManifest and ScenarioRunner replay recorded steps with fixed dates; QualityProfile levels carry resolution, element, iteration and effect-pass shares; QualityGovernor and FramePacing step quality and frame cap down under heat and Low Power Mode; ParticleSystem has a fixed capacity; DocumentStore.maxBytes and StorageQuota bound storage.

matrix.capability: Shader backgrounds: procedural full-screen backgrounds drawn by bundled GLSL over the canvas through RenderHost, with named uniforms, a palette of colour stops and the vc/ noise, SDF, hash and colour library; fields for flowing backgrounds

matrix.source: brainstorm: animation; manual §6 rule: display animation time is never the wall clock
matrix.notes: Tested in SceneClockTests, FullScreenShaderSceneTests (fixedTime), ParticleSystemTests, ParticleLayerSceneTests, ParticleRendererTests and AccessibilityPreferencesTests. FullScreenShaderScene.timeScale is public but no test names it (grep 2026-11-16), so the themes drive time through SceneClock and fixedTime. The wall clock never drives animation (M12).

matrix.capability: Typography integration: the time and date drawn as native text with system fonts over the shader background, legible on every theme, laid out for portrait and landscape and for 12/24 hours with and without seconds
matrix.source: brainstorm: typography integration; manual §6 rule 3 (text in native UI over the background)
matrix.notes: Framework part tested: CanvasOverlayTests (a presenter's overlay reaches the shell; the host view builds with and without one) and AccessibilitySettingsSectionTests (contrastRatio). No text is drawn in the GPU path, by design: the overlay keeps the time readable when rendering pauses or fails (manual §6). matrix.capability: Scene transitions: switching themes with a short crossfade between two full-screen scenes (a cut under Reduce Motion), without a frame of black and without rebuilding the clock text

matrix.notes: Tested in RenderHostTests and ShellLifecycleTests (replaceScene), ResourceRegistryTests, FieldPassTests and AccessibilityPlansTests (transitionDuration). replaceScene and Generative Art Studio's ArtCanvasScene swap scenes as a hard cut; no crossfade exists in any framework product (grep 2026-11-16). No keep-awake API exists in a framework product and no experience sets isIdleTimerDisabled today. matrix.capability: Experience host: session, shell, presenter with the canvas overlay, feedback and scenario runner in the one app, no new target
matrix.source: ADR-0009; spec FR-A18-005
matrix.notes: Tested in SessionOpenCloseTests, ShellLifecycleTests, ShellRenderingTests, CanvasOverlayTests and ScenarioRunnerTests.

matrix.capability: Determinism and GPU-free testability: the same preferences, theme and injected date give the same state digest and the same text; formatting, documents, night-mode and motion rules and the schedule are pure models tested with swift test
matrix.source: constitution A18 testable without the GPU
matrix.notes: Tested in StateDigestTests, ExperienceSnapshotTests and the ScenarioManifestTests. The injected date is G-CLOCK.

gaps.justification: No framework product offers a wall-clock source or time-change observation. An injectable clock (system by default, fixed in tests) that also reports foreground return, significant time change, time-zone and locale changes has two consumers (A14's Now and A18), so it is assessed for VisualCoreExperience in A18-P01 (the observation side, needing UIKit notifications, in VisualCoreExperienceHost if required). If the assessment keeps it app-local, the experience implements the same contract in its Core without copying Solar System Explorer's code. The production path never offsets or simulates time.
gaps.test: Host tests with a fixed clock: the source returns the injected date; each notification (foreground, significant time change, time zone, locale) emits one change event; the default reads the system clock; API baseline and documentation updated if it lands in VisualCore; the seven-step reference regression passes

gaps.justification: ClockPreferences (12/24 hours or system, seconds, calendar, time-zone and locale policy) and the formatter over Foundation's Calendar, Locale, TimeZone and DateFormatter, plus the next-tick deadline on second or minute boundaries, are the clock's domain (manual phase 01).
gaps.test: Core host tests with fixed dates: 12/24 hours in en_US, de_DE, ja_JP and ar; seconds on and off; the DST spring-forward and fall-back hours in a fixed zone; a time-zone change; midnight rollover; next-tick deadlines on boundaries; invalid preferences refused

gaps.justification: The time spoken in full, the VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type sizes for the clock text and the announcement policy are the experience's UI over the public planners (manual phase 01).
gaps.test: Core tests: the spoken string names the time with its period or 24-hour form and the date when shown for each test locale; no minute change announces; time.speak bursts are rate-limited by AnnouncementPlanner at 0.5 s (the overlay label at every Dynamic Type size is tested with G-OVERLAY, A18-P02)

gaps.justification: The native clock overlay (through makeCanvasOverlay), its layouts for portrait and landscape, the contrast rule against the theme's palette and the first shader theme (noise gradient) are app work over the public overlay and FullScreenShaderScene (manual phase 02). It also holds the presenter that reads the clock source, sends time.set at each scheduled deadline and time.changed from TimeChangeMonitor.applicationNames, and gives the canvas the spoken string as its accessibility label at every Dynamic Type size (moved here from G-TIMEA11Y at A18-P01, whose part is the core).
gaps.test: Core tests: the contrast ratio of the text against every palette stop of the first theme is at least 4.5 (contrastRatio); experience tests: the overlay shows the formatted time over a rendered frame; the text stays when the scene fails to compile

gaps.justification: Resolution share, iteration and particle counts per quality tier for each theme are the experience's numbers over QualityLevel, ParticleSystem.capacity and ResourceBudget.
gaps.test: Experience tests (A18-P02): Core.qualityTiers is 2 with level-0 and level-1; fixed noise octaves 5 and 3 and pixel blocks 1 and 2 per level; one full-screen draw per frame; speeds outside 0.25-2 refused; frames at both levels not blank (theme presets and their budgets come with A18-P03)

gaps.justification: The other three themes (particle drift, wave field, SDF shapes), the ThemePreset model with its quality and motion controls, the built-in presets and their license entries are content (manual phase 03).
gaps.test: Core tests: four themes, each with valid presets inside declared ranges; experience tests: every theme compiles and renders a frame at every tier; each shader has a license entry

gaps.justification: replaceScene is a hard cut and no crossfade exists. A generic crossfade between two full-screen scenes (both rendered into render targets, mixed by a pass over a duration, cut under Reduce Motion) has consumers beyond A18 (Generative Art Studio switches families with a cut), so it is assessed for VisualCoreRendering in A18-P03 as an additive scene; existing scenes are unchanged. If not promoted, the experience composes it from public render targets and FieldPass; never a second renderer. Promoted at A18-P03 as VisualCoreRendering's CrossfadeScene (feature 133), with CrossfadeSceneTests.
gaps.test: Rendering tests: the mix at t=0 equals scene A, at t=1 scene B, midway the average within tolerance; no black frame; resize and context loss rebuild both targets; transitionDuration gives a cut under Reduce Motion; reference regression passes

gaps.justification: The theme document (schema version, validation, migration), the editor and the favourites count cap are the experience's, stored in a NamedLibrary in its ExperienceStorage (manual phase 03).
gaps.test: Core tests: a theme round-trips; an older schema migrates; damaged, oversized or newer documents are refused without a crash; the cap refuses one more favourite; names normalised

gaps.justification: Night mode (manual or scheduled, dim level, warm or red palette, lower brightness cap, contrast floor) is drawn in the scene; the system screen brightness is never set (spec clarification 4; manual phase 04).
gaps.test: Core tests: night palettes keep contrast at least 4.5 with the text; brightness never above the cap; the schedule switches at its boundaries with fixed dates; a source scan finds no UIScreen brightness write

gaps.justification: The motion-reduction option and Reduce Motion still the animated themes (SceneClock speed and reducedMotion, a still frame or very slow drift) as the experience's policy over AccessibilityPreferences.
gaps.test: Core tests: with motion reduced the animation clock does not advance beyond the still rule; the system setting and the in-app option resolve through AccessibilityPreferences; transitions cut

gaps.justification: An experience cannot lower its frame cap: ExperienceSession creates RenderHost with the default maxFramesPerSecond. An experience-declared cap (never below FramePacing.minimumFPS) is generic and is assessed for VisualCoreExperienceHost in A18-P04, additive with the default unchanged for every other experience. Promoted at A18-P04 as ExperiencePresenter.maxFramesPerSecond and Experience.maxFramesPerSecond (VisualCoreExperienceHost, feature 134), with FrameCapTests.
gaps.test: Host tests: a declared cap reaches host.framePacing.maxFPS; the default stays 60; Low Power Mode and heat still lower it; API baseline updated; reference regression passes

gaps.justification: A slow, bounded pixel drift of the text and scene and an idle dimming are the experience's screen-care policy (manual §13 risk 1); Digital Aquarium's AmbientDimmer is not copied, and a generic drift is assessed for VisualCoreSimulation in this phase only if a second consumer exists.
gaps.test: Core tests with fixed dates: the drift offset stays within its bound, moves at most its rate per minute and is deterministic; dimming starts after the idle interval and a touch restores; Reduce Motion keeps the drift below its visible step

gaps.justification: The opt-in keep-awake setting (off by default) sets isIdleTimerDisabled only while the clock is visible, in exactly one named file of the experience, and releases it on background, close and teardown; the privacy page says so (spec clarification 4).
gaps.test: Experience tests with an injected idle-timer port: on only when the setting is on and the clock is visible; off on background, close and teardown; a source scan finds isIdleTimerDisabled in exactly one file

gaps.justification: Overnight device tests (plugged in and on battery), thermal and frame-pacing records and the QA rows belong to the device campaign after ImplementationLock-100 (manual phase 05); device actions by the owner are BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION. Planned at A18-P05 in docs/apps/ambient-clock/device-campaign.md (AC-D1 to AC-D10, every row pending until ImplementationLock-100); the simulator-side fixture that a still picture is drawn once is VisualCoreRendering's CachedScene (feature 135).

negative.rule: Risk 1, thermal load and OLED burn-in over long sessions. Owner: Ambient Clock screen care and budgets (app-local G-SCREENCARE, G-NIGHT and G-BUDGETS; G-FRAMERATE in VisualCoreExperienceHost assessed in A18-P04) with the overnight device runs in A18-P05 (G-DEVICE). Verification: host tests bound the drift offset and rate, the dimming schedule, the brightness cap and every tier's budget; the night tier asks for a lower frame cap; the overnight device run records thermal state and frame pacing. Release blocker: a static, undimmed layout over a long session, a drift outside its bound, a theme over its tier budget, or a performance, battery or thermal claim without a device measurement.

Risk 2, time correctness errors break trust. Owner: the clock source and formatter (G-CLOCK in VisualCoreExperience assessed in A18-P01; app-local G-FORMAT in A18-P01). Verification: host tests with fixed dates cover 12/24 hours in several locales, DST spring-forward and fall-back, time-zone and locale changes, midnight and significant time change, and the next-tick schedule; a source scan finds no Date() or clock read outside the injected source in the production path. Release blocker: any wrong formatted time in the fixtures, a missed update after a time change or foreground return, or a simulated or offset clock in the production path.

Risk 3, weather implies permissions and data terms. Owner: Ambient Clock release (G-RELEASE in A18-P06); weather is out of version 0.1. Verification: the dependency and usage-description checks find no location, network or weather API and no usage string added for A18; the copy-claims step refuses weather and forecast wording. Release blocker: any location or network use, any new usage string, or any weather claim in the experience, its copy or the store text.

reasons: A working host and a buildable text-over-shader path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal draws FullScreenShaderScene, FieldPass and ParticleLayerScene over the vc/ GLSL library, and ExperiencePresenter.makeCanvasOverlay puts native SwiftUI text over the canvas, all public and tested (FullScreenShaderSceneTests, FieldPassTests, ParticleLayerSceneTests, CanvasOverlayTests); Simulation Lab already combines FieldPass drawing with a canvas overlay on it, and Generative Art Studio, Fractal Explorer and Digital Aquarium draw full-screen shader scenes.

9 of 28 rows are available with tests: shader backgrounds, animation, the canvas overlay for text, favourites with schema and migration, quality tiers, lifecycle with resize and context loss, licenses, the experience host and determinism.

All 19 non-available rows have owned gaps: G-CLOCK (VisualCoreExperience assessed, second consumer A14), G-FORMAT and G-TIMEA11Y in A18-P01; G-OVERLAY and G-BUDGETS in A18-P02; G-THEMES, G-FAVOURITES and the additive VisualCoreRendering crossfade G-TRANSITION in A18-P03; G-NIGHT, G-MOTION, G-SCREENCARE, G-AWAKE and the additive VisualCoreExperienceHost frame cap G-FRAMERATE in A18-P04; G-DEVICE in A18-P05; G-RELEASE in A18-P06. No upstream change is needed to start.

No permission and no privacy answer changes; the only platform exception is the opt-in keep-awake in one named file (G-AWAKE, G-RELEASE). Ambient Clock stays unregistered (17 registered, A01-A17) until A18-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/AmbientClock with its targets and first real rules.
